objectives: Get ready for bed in the right order.
Say the bedtime words to your family.
Talk about your day before you sleep.
Use the words for bedtime, routine and pajamas.
Prepare your school bag and clothes for tomorrow.
Calm down when you cannot fall asleep.

sections.body:
Bedtime is the part of the day when you stop being busy and start resting. Your body knows it is coming. That is why your eyes get heavy at the same time every evening.

A **bedtime routine** is a set of steps you do in the same order every night. A bath. Then teeth. Then pyjamas. Then a story. Then bed.

Why does the order matter? Because your brain learns it. After a few weeks, the sound of running water is enough to make you feel sleepy. You do not have to think about it.

A good routine is calm and predictable. It should take about 30 minutes. It should end with something warm: a story, a song, or a chat with your family.

And there is one more job of bedtime. It is the best time of the day to talk to your parents. The lights are low, everybody is tired, and words come out easier.

In this article you will learn the order of the routine, the words you need for bedtime, and what to do on the nights when sleep will not come.
examples: Can I have one more story?
sections.heading: What bedtime is, and why a routine helps

sections.body:
A school night is a chain. Each link depends on the one before it.

**After school**, put your bag in the same place every day. A bag by the door is a bag that gets packed. A bag on the floor is a bag that gets forgotten.

**At dinner**, talk about your day. One good question is enough: *What was the best part of your day?* You will hear things you never heard before.

**After dinner**, do the quiet things. Homework, then a bath. Not a bath in the middle of homework, or homework in your pyjamas. The order keeps your body and your brain in the right place.

**In the last half hour**, slow down. Turn the lights down. Put the screens away. A bright screen tells your brain it is still daytime.

**In bed**, the day is finished. No more homework, no more games. If something is unfinished, write it on a piece of paper for tomorrow. Then it can wait.
examples: What was the best part of your day?
Let me pack my bag first.
I will write it down for tomorrow.
sections.heading: The evening, hour by hour

sections.body:
These are the words you need at the end of the day. Learn them and you can talk about bedtime in two languages.

**Bedtime** is the time when you get ready to sleep. *It is bedtime* means the evening is over.

**A routine** is a set of things you do in the same order every time. Your morning is a routine too: brush teeth, get dressed, eat breakfast.

**Pyjamas** are the soft clothes you wear in bed. In Vietnamese we call them *đồ ngủ*.

**To brush your teeth** means to clean them with a toothbrush and toothpaste, usually for two minutes.

**Good night** is what you say to somebody when you go to bed. In Vietnamese, children say *Chúc con ngủ ngon* or *Ngủ ngon*.

**To fall asleep** means to go from being awake to being asleep. It is not something you do. It is something that happens to you.

A **nightlight** is a small dim lamp you leave on so the room is not completely dark.
examples: I brush my teeth after my bath.
sections.heading: The bedtime words, one by one

terms.example: Bedtime is eight o'clock on a school night.
terms.gloss: The time when you get ready to sleep. It is the end of the evening.

terms.example: Our bedtime routine is the same every night.
terms.gloss: A set of things you do in the same order every time. A bedtime routine helps your body get sleepy.

terms.example: I put on my pyjamas before I brush my teeth.
terms.gloss: The soft clothes you wear in bed.

terms.example: I brush my teeth before I put on my pyjamas.
terms.gloss: To clean your teeth with a toothbrush and toothpaste, usually for two minutes.

terms.example: I say good night to my grandmother every night.
terms.gloss: What you say to somebody when you go to bed. It is a wish for a deep sleep.

sections.body:
Here is the routine that works. Do it in this order and it takes about half an hour.

First, pack your school bag. Put tomorrow's things in it now.

Then take your bath or shower. This is the part your body remembers.

Next, brush your teeth. Two minutes, all the way round.

Then put on your pyjamas and get into bed.

After that, read one story, or talk for a while, or sing a song.

Finally, say good night, turn off the big light, and leave the nightlight if you need it.

If you do the same order every night, your body will get sleepy all by itself. You will not need to be told.
examples: My bag is packed, so I am ready for tomorrow.
Two minutes, then my teeth are clean.
Good night, see you in the morning.
sections.heading: How to get ready for bed
steps: Pack your school bag for tomorrow.
Take a bath or a shower.
Brush your teeth for two minutes.
Put on your pyjamas and get into bed.
Read one story and say good night.

sections.body:
The last half hour of the day is a special time. This is when a child says things they would not say at breakfast.

**Say good night properly.** *Good night. I love you.* Three short sentences, every night. They are not silly. They are the glue of the day.

**Share one thing from your day.** Not the whole day. One thing. *A new girl said hello to me today.* A child learns that adults listen, because they do.

**Ask about their day too.** *How was your day, Mum?* Grown-ups need this as well.

**Tell them if you are worried.** A worry is lighter when you say it out loud in a dark room. Sometimes a worry is just about tomorrow's maths test.

**Ask for comfort if you need it.** A glass of water, a little more light, one more song. Asking for what you need is a skill, not a weakness.

**Make it warm and small.** A story in a cosy room beats a loud television every single night.
examples: Good night. I love you very much.
I am a little worried about tomorrow.
sections.heading: Talking with your family before bed

sections.body:
Some nights you lie in the dark and sleep does not come. That is normal. It happens to everybody, even grown-ups.

**Keep your body tired and your room dark.** Daylight and bright screens at night tell your brain it is still morning.

**Do not look at the clock.** Watching the time makes waiting worse. Read a book instead.

**Breathe slowly.** Breathe in while you count to four, and out while you count to six. Do it five times. Your body cannot stay excited while you breathe like that.

**Think about something boring.** A slow walk through a long list. Counting sheep is old, but it works because it is boring.

**If you are still awake after a while, get up.** Sit somewhere dim and read. When you feel sleepy, go back to bed.

And if you are scared, or your head aches, or you cannot breathe, tell an adult straight away. That is what they are there for.
examples: I will read a book until I feel sleepy.
My head hurts. Can you sit with me?
sections.heading: On the nights when sleep will not come

item.summary: Bedtime is a routine, and a routine is a set of small steps you repeat every night. After reading this you can get ready for bed in the right order, say the bedtime words, talk with your family before sleep, and calm down when you cannot fall asleep.
